name: Axonex
description: Axonex triggers a prolonged state of heightened neural plasticity by upregulating BDNF, CREB, and related synaptic growth factors, recreating in adults the rapid-learning neurochemical environment of childhood development. During its window, new motor skills, procedural knowledge, and technical competencies are acquired at two to three times normal speed. Originally developed for post-injury motor rehabilitation, it was rapidly adopted by the professional training market.
effects: 2-3x acceleration of motor and procedural skill acquisition
Dramatically enhanced response to deliberate practice
Faster formation of technical and conceptual schemas
Heightened receptivity to instruction and demonstration
Improved cross-domain transfer of learned skills
side_effects: Indiscriminate plasticity — bad habits and misinformation learned as fast as correct content
Vulnerability to manipulation and social influence during dose window
Muscular soreness from accelerated motor learning
Long-term: plasticity rebound — learning speed drops below baseline for weeks after heavy use
cultural_context: Axonex has transformed vocational training in GLMZ. Corporate onboarding programs that once took months now take weeks. Combat training academies use it for weapons familiarization. The dark side is that the indiscriminate plasticity effect means Axonex users during their dose window are profoundly susceptible to manipulation — cults, criminal organizations, and certain corporate HR programs have been documented using Axonex environments to instill loyalty and behavioral conditioning. On Tier 1, it's used by people trying to rapidly acquire marketable skills to escape the Shelf.
story_hooks: A Shelf resident has been using black-market Axonex to rapidly train himself in cybersecurity skills, learning in months what takes others years — but his dealer has been lacing the supply with a behavioral conditioning compound, and the skills he's learning come pre-packaged with loyalty to someone he's never met.

A corporate training facility is under investigation after former employees report that their Axonex-assisted onboarding included undisclosed psychological conditioning — they all share inexplicable brand loyalty and emotional distress when thinking critically about the company.

A street rumor claims there's a teacher on Tier 1 who runs Axonex learning sessions in an abandoned school — free of charge, no conditioning, just pure skill transfer. Someone wants her found and shut down.
